headline: AI-powered platforms capturing consumer relationships and economic moats as intermediaries.

deltas.metric: Affirm Card GMV and cardholder adoption
deltas.to: Q3 2026: GMV grew 146% to $2.1B; active cardholders more than doubled to 4.4M
deltas.reads: AI-driven underwriting and merchant conversion logic embedding direct payment relationship between consumer and platform, bypassing card network intermediaries.

deltas.metric: AI customer-support resolution rate and cost efficiency
deltas.to: Q2 2026: AI assistant resolved 45% of issues without human agent; support cost per booking declined 16% YoY
deltas.reads: AI-native customer support removing human agent as relationship touchpoint and cost center, compressing service margin.

deltas.metric: AI-enabled agentic commerce and premium card adoption
deltas.to: Q2 2026: management explicitly highlighted agentic-commerce tooling; Millennial/Gen Z became largest share of U.S. consumer spending; net card fee revenue posted 30th straight quarter of double-digit growth
deltas.change: +30 consecutive quarters double-digit card fee growth
deltas.reads: AI agents discovering products and completing payments without human advisor intermediation, capturing payment authority and data that professionals formerly controlled.

deltas.to: Q2 2026: take rate 25.9%; take-rate expansion led by Etsy Ads and on-site monetization
deltas.reads: Platform monetization expanding beyond merchant fees into ads and algorithmic promotion layer, capturing economic value sellers once controlled directly.

deltas.metric: AI-driven diagnostic decision-making and test adoption
deltas.from: 2024: established Cologuard franchise with physician referral model
deltas.to: 2025: launched three new tests (Cancerguard, Oncodetect, blood-based CRC); full-year revenue $3.25B; screened more people than ever
deltas.change: +3 new AI-optimized tests in 2025; revenue growth continuing
deltas.reads: AI diagnostic systems making triage and screening decisions formerly reserved for physician judgment, disintermediating clinical authority through direct-to-consumer testing access.

deltas.metric: Knowledge intermediary contract value under AI pressure
deltas.to: Q2 2026: revenue $100.2M (-10.1% YoY); contract value $283.2M (down 3% YoY); management highlighted Forrester AI adoption
deltas.reads: Legacy research intermediary losing pricing power and contract value as AI provides alternative judgment layer; company pivoting to embed AI workflows to defend intermediation moat.

deltas.to: Q2 2026: contract value $5.3B, up 1.7% YoY (FX-neutral); Insights client retention 85%; management said contract-value growth accelerated
deltas.reads: Institutional research intermediary holding pricing moat despite AI competition because workflow integration and executive prioritization remain sticky even as information abundance rises.

momentum_note: The trend is accelerating across two distinct mechanisms: (1) Consumer-facing platforms (Affirm, Airbnb, AmEx, Etsy, Exact) are using AI to directly capture economic relationships, pricing power, and decision-making authority that intermediaries—financial advisors, travel agents, copywriters, diagnostic specialists—formerly held. Card attachment, support resolution, take-rate expansion, and test adoption all show platforms compressing the intermediary layer. (2) Knowledge and labor intermediaries (Forrester, Gartner, Korn Ferry) face mixed pressure: Forrester lost pricing power as AI provides alternative judgment; Gartner and Korn Ferry hold moats through workflow integration and remaining-fee growth, suggesting that institutional intermediaries can survive by embedding themselves into client systems rather than selling periodic reports or placements alone. The structural shift is that AI improves with each decision, compounding the moat faster than human intermediaries can close the gap.
